//counts: Measured 2026-10-10 after routing the scribe into SOAP: 2185/1443/735/7 with NO database, and 2185/2180/0/5 against a local PostgreSQL 17.10. +3 over the consent-gate figures, all three database-free, so the SKIPPED ceiling did not move. Client 367. THE RULE DID NOT CHANGE; IT MOVED TO THE RIGHT PLACE. The scribe used to draft the Subjective and nothing else, on the rule that a model drafting an assessment is a model making a clinical decision. That rule stands. What was wrong is WHERE it sat: when a pharmacist says out loud "chest is clear, looks viral, honey and fluids, come back in five days", the assessment and the plan were MADE BY A PERSON, and writing them into the right boxes is transcription. Refusing was not safety, it was making a pharmacist retype a decision they had already spoken. So the line moved from WHICH SECTION to WHOSE WORDS: the patient’s voice drafts Subjective and nothing else, the pharmacist’s drafts Objective, Assessment and Plan, and a voice that said nothing drafts nothing. The structured records (problems, interventions, referral, prescription, care-program, summary) stay forbidden, and now for a sharper reason: they are not prose but records with their own validation and their own audit trail. ONE model call with both halves labelled, because the owner asked for swift and this deployment’s model reasons for seconds - but the labelling is a HINT and each section is then validated against the words of the person who owns it, so a model that files the pharmacist’s advice as the patient’s report is caught rather than trusted. A NEW REFUSAL, hardenedACertainty: an assessment that drops a hedge the pharmacist used. "I think it MIGHT be viral" filed as "Viral upper respiratory infection" has turned a working impression into a diagnosis and the next reader cannot tell. Asked only of the Assessment, because that is the section where certainty IS the clinical content. WITHINTRANSCRIPT BECAME A RATIO, and this is a LOOSENING named as one. The first live run refused the Subjective as longer_than_transcript at 462 characters from 444 of speech - FOUR PER CENT over, on the normal case, for the most important section. Measured: subjective 1.04, objective 0.21, assessment 0.24, plan 0.44, because the Subjective covers ALL of a patient’s speech while the others cover part of the pharmacist’s. Capped at 1.5 now. It still catches a model answering a short recording with paragraphs; it never caught a fabricated symptom that fits inside the budget, at any threshold, because that is SHORTER - which needs entity-level grounding and has its own task. Six mutations run against the new safety logic and all six turned the right test red. TWO EXISTING INVARIANTS WERE AMENDED WITH THE PRODUCT, NOT RELAXED. scribeContract’s pinned SCRIBABLE === [subjective]; it now pins the stronger claim that every section is drafted from the voice that owns it AND that a forbidden section has no owning voice at all. consultationLayout’s microphone invariant pinned an early return the mode machine replaced; it now pins REACHABILITY - the microphone is opened in exactly one place, that place renders only under mode ready, and ready is reachable only via a consented note or the server’s own acceptance of consent. Measured again 2026-10-11 after adding counter patient creation: 2192/1450/735/7 with NO database and 2192/2187/0/5 with one. +7, all database-free, so the skipped ceiling did not move. The feature is an INSERT NOBODY WROTE: the route calls customerIdentity.resolveCustomer, the existing upsert that is atomic by constraint, rather than inserting into customers itself - because identity_key is unique per pharmacy and a hand-written INSERT would have worked today and produced a DUPLICATE the first time that person texted. Proven against a real database: 0803 999 1122 typed at the counter creates (201); +2348039991122 returns the SAME id with created:false (200); and the same number arriving over WhatsApp resolves to that same row, leaving ONE row for the identity, with the pharmacist's full_name surviving while display_name becomes what WhatsApp calls them (the 0020 split). A PHONE NUMBER IS REQUIRED and that is a schema fact: wa_jid is NOT NULL (0016) and identity_key is NOT NULL (0019). A walk-in with NO phone is therefore not supported, and supporting one means making wa_jid nullable, which is a change to the live identity path and belongs in its own commit. wa_jid is synthesised as <number>@s.whatsapp.net and overwritten with the real one on first message; nothing can send to it meanwhile because messageInput's outreach gate refuses a patient who has not written first. 8 mutations run and the EIGHTH WAS MISSED, which taught something: deleting the required-phone check still refuses an empty box, falling through to the parser and saying "that does not look like a phone number" - safe, and wrong for the person, because an empty field is not a malformed one. The test now asserts the MESSAGE and the mutation then failed.

SHELL_PLAN.md phase 4 (2026-10-11): the chrome names the patient, and the line under it says nothing rather than something false. NOT THE PHASE THAT WAS PLANNED. The plan said these seven screens would take the new surface and spacing "mechanically and wide"; opened on the new shell and measured, they already had it - the warm page is a global token they inherited in phase 1, the record nav is already 12px, and the Meds section already has two rounded containers. Restyling seven screens against no named defect would have been a wide diff that fixed nothing. WHAT WAS WRONG WAS THE CHROME, in three places at once: standing in Ngozi Okafor’s medication record the breadcrumb said "Patients / All patients", the heading said "Patients", and the subtitle said "View all your customers’ details". All three describe the screen you LEFT, and on a clinical record the name at the top is the thing a pharmacist checks before acting. SHIPPED IN TWO COMMITS BECAUSE THE FIRST WAS NOT FINISHED. a932d33 fixed the heading and the breadcrumb and left the subtitle - the same lie one line lower, on all nine sections of the record - and it shipped with NO TEST AT ALL, which AGENTS.md forbids. This commit carries the subtitle and the tests for both halves. THE SUBTITLE IS ABSENT ON A RECORD, NOT REPLACED, and the element is not rendered rather than rendered empty: everything a subtitle could honestly say there is already on screen and said better (the record nav highlights the section, the identity card carries age, sex and number, the allergy banner carries the one fact worth reading before acting), a fourth copy would be noise, and an empty

reads as something that failed to load. THE GUARD THAT MAKES THAT SAFE IS ITS OWN TEST: pageSubtitle is nullable now, so a screen that lost its SUBTITLE entry would quietly render nothing and look deliberate. Every screen the sidebar can open is asserted to have one, read from modules.js rather than a fixture, so the only thing the condition can suppress is the case it was written for. THE NAME COMES FROM THE ROW THAT WAS CLICKED, not a second request - PatientSearch already hands the patient over beside the id, and asking the server again for something just shown is how two answers to one question appear. A patient opened by deep link arrives with no name and the heading stays "Patients": vague, which is honest, rather than wrong. NULL ON THE WAY BACK is covered twice on purpose - the back button is the path a person takes, the effect keyed to selectedId is what holds when the record closes some other way. A heading still carrying a patient’s name after you have left their record is confidently wrong rather than merely vague. VERIFIED ON THE RUNNING SCREEN in both directions, across all nine sections; the first commit said plainly that it had not been, and it had not. Nine mutations run, nine of the right tests red. Client 361 -> 367. No server file was touched, so the server counts are unchanged.
